narrative_obligations.detail: Trust must change through earned cooperation, not instant friendship.
The compass must ultimately remain lost rather than be replaced by a reward.

artifact.prose:
Below the dry section of the stair, storm water churned across the lower room. The dragon hatchling crouched on the ledge just above it, trembling whenever the waves struck the sea grate.

Ekin stared down at the small creature. Her brass compass was gone because she had chased after it. Worse, the chase had left the hatchling trapped here while its mother waited above, unable to squeeze down the narrow stair.

“This is my fault,” Ekin said. Her voice shook, but she forced herself to look at Duru. “I frightened it down there. I’m getting it back up.”

Duru watched her for a moment, then nodded. “I’ll help.”

“I can manage.”

Another wave crashed through the grate. Water surged beneath the ledge, and the hatchling pressed itself flat.

Ekin pulled off her jacket. Lying on the dry stair, she stretched toward the ledge and held the jacket open between her hands. The hatchling backed away at first.

“Easy,” Ekin whispered. “I won’t hurt you.”

She lowered the jacket over its back and gathered it gently around the cat-sized body. The hatchling squirmed, making Ekin’s arms wobble.

Duru dropped beside her. She had seen exactly what Ekin was trying to do. “Pass it to me. You’ll need both hands to stand.”

Ekin hesitated. The hatchling twisted again, dangerously close to slipping from her grasp.

“All right,” she said.

Duru braced herself on the dry stair and reached down. Ekin lifted the jacket-wrapped hatchling into her arms. Duru held it firmly against her while Ekin rose.

“Got it?” Ekin asked.

“I’ve got it.”

Ekin studied Duru’s careful grip, then gave one reluctant nod. “Thanks. That was—good thinking.”

Together they climbed the narrow stair, taking each step slowly while the storm battered the lighthouse. Duru carried the hatchling, and Ekin kept one hand beneath the bundled creature whenever it wriggled.

They returned to the upper room with the hatchling safe between them. Ekin did not call Duru a friend. Not yet. But she no longer watched her like a stranger who had no right to help.
